entry.title: Not the Agent’s Word: Checking What an AI Agent Says It Did Against What the Platform Saw
entry.summary: Whitepaper on anchorstamp (18 pages, PDF). An AI agent’s record of what it did is written by the agent; anchorstamp checks it against an observer the agent cannot reach, a Linux kernel module whose records are anchored in a TPM. Results from one laptop, and every limit with the control that would close it.

entry.title: The Agent Was Never the Recorder (Below the API, Part 2)
entry.summary: Part 1 ended at a runtime that refuses to record. This part takes the recording obligation away from the agent: claim, observe, join, verdict, and what one laptop showed. On Medium.

entry.title: From virgl to zero-copy gfxstream
entry.summary: Moving an Android Automotive guest from virgl to gfxstream on an Arm SoC whose hypervisor cannot share host memory at runtime: three compatibility contracts, zero copy from guest memory, and per-frame attribution of virtualisation overhead.

entry.title: Case study: GPU virtualisation for a software-defined vehicle cockpit
entry.summary: Moving an Android Automotive guest from virgl to gfxstream, with Vulkan, GLES through ANGLE and zero-copy rendering from guest memory, then optimising it to the customer’s performance targets.

entry.title: From chain of trust to chain of timing
entry.summary: A position paper for Physical AI: access, trust and time contracts at every boundary on a shared SoC, the SPDM/IDE trust chain as a template for a chain of timing, where timing breaks hop by hop, and proposals by community.

entry.title: From specification to silicon: the SPDM/IDE trust chain
entry.summary: How DICE identity, SPDM attestation and IDE link protection compose into a verifiable trust chain for confidential computing. First published on LinkedIn in April 2026; now the canonical copy, with dated corrections.

entry.title: Case study: QNX and Linux cockpit displays on one PC
entry.summary: vcockpit composes a QNX 8.0 instrument cluster and a Linux guest, each in its own virtual machine, into one cockpit display on a PC, so cockpit software can be built and integrated before vehicle hardware exists. Open source, with a codelab.

entry.title: VirtIO and hypervisors: how virtual devices work
entry.summary: A technical reference on device virtualisation: emulation, VirtIO and assignment; virtqueues and notifications; KVM with vhost, vhost-user and vDPA; Xen grants and IOREQ; QNX, L4Re and Gunyah; VFIO; pKVM and Arm CCA; and virtio-msg.

entry.title: Mixed-criticality on shared silicon: a primer for Physical AI
entry.summary: Where tail latency comes from when AI inference and real-time control share an SoC, why partial isolation falls short, two isolation architectures, measurement discipline, and the EU compliance dates that make it urgent.

entry.title: Case study: TEE trusted services for an automotive telematics unit
entry.summary: Hardened TLS, secure storage and secure logging in OP-TEE for a 5G telematics control unit, toward UN R155 and ISO/SAE 21434 compliance.

entry.title: Case study: secure video streaming for in-flight entertainment
entry.summary: Widevine L1 DRM and aviation-qualified secure boot on NXP i.MX8, designed for certification from day one.
